patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Office Timeline and Todoist share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Office Timeline and Todoist share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose Office Timeline only if your buying job matches “PowerPoint-native timeline / Gantt specialist (now Lucen Timeline) — Free add-in; Lite fro” rather than Todoist's shape. Choose Todoist only if your buying job matches “Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/” rather than Office Timeline's shape. Workflow advantage: Office Timeline leans timeline-reporting; Todoist leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Office Timeline and Todoist share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Office Timeline is PowerPoint-native timeline / Gantt specialist (now Lucen Timeline) — Free add-in; Lite from $9/user/mo annual.; Todoist is Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/mo annual; Business ~$10..
- Company-size focus: Office Timeline (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Todoist (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Office Timeline-leaning timeline-reporting vs Todoist-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Office Timeline — Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management; Todoist — Not a Work OS or portfolio tool.

Limitations — Office Timeline: Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management; Centre of gravity is PowerPoint presentation timelines, not live team task execution; Todoist: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool; Team features mainly on Business.

Poor-fit cases: Office Timeline is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management · Todoist is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool · Avoid Office Timeline if you actually need Todoist's motion (Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
